posts.title: Cannon Cove, Lego 6266: A Fresh Review
posts.text: I recently pieced together a pirate version of Cannon Cove that I will eventually position close to Rock Island Refuge or Forbidden Island when I rebuild my larger pirate base of operations. I think this will go nicely with either of those two, especially Rock Island Refuge, which I envision to be a dilapidated and abandoned imperial fort. This is a nice extension of it. Where I didn't have a suitable original style piece I simply swapped for what was available. This arched window is a good example: I do have a few of the BURP pieces but I'm saving those for a bigger project in my display, so I sort of threw together a few brick-built rocks and another arched window for this side: You've got Burried Treasure in the foreground and to the left we have everyone's favorite pirate captain enjoying a much needed break from the pillaging and plundering that typically fills his days. This is actually from the Pirates of Barnacle Bay and if you recall it is actually Ironhook who comes with this build. These sets, all placed on a Forbidden Island printed baseplate, are a temporary "throw together" until I can craft a more permanent pirate hideout. And of course, the pirate version of Cannon Cove will be a part of that. These additional shanties will probably also find their way into it. For now the Cannon Cove build is the focus and this dark version of it underscores the simplicity and epic interchangeability of these old vintage sets.

posts.title: Attempting to build a skid steer with 3+ wheels, need advice
posts.text: I've built a few skid steer chassis with wheels/tracks. Do not use differentials. If you're using 3 wheels on each side, I'd recommend putting drive on only the middle wheel and leaving the others as free wheel. I found with 4x4 skids, the best turning and handling was when i only had drive on the rear wheels.

posts.title: Using Claude AI for new ports and translations
posts.text: Claude is working now on reinforcement learning algorithm directly processed by logo on a line follower, it already finished one version and trying to improve it. Here is the last version. https://htmlhoster.com/p/P4HMYAEN/ "I've improved the Logo learning example (Version 99, same link), so you can now see the buggy learn. Progress: Each TRAIN prints the average reward per step. In my run over six trainings it rose from −0.53 to −0.03. Result: After that, DRIVE followed the oval for 40 sampled seconds without leaving the line. This was one real-time run, so it shows the idea works, not how often. POLICY: This is a new command. It prints what the buggy would do in each state it has met, for example "state 0 -> forward" or "state 12 -> right". The state numbers are explained in the program's comments. Fixed: Longer training runs hit the interpreter's limit on nested calls. They are now plain loops. The usual caveat applies: press Reset machine before each command, and results vary a little from one try to the next because the buggy explores at random."

posts.title: [Help] [Wip] ball launcher for GBC
posts.text: There's a lot of forces involved getting the ball up that high consistently. The axle would even go up higher, or the ball gets jammed, without the rubber gate. I'm running the same tire for about 30 event days, and no visible wear can be seen. Your suggested wheel can also work with the right gearing to get the ball high enough for your purpose, but the tire cannot flex to accomedate for ball dimension fluctuation since it is solid. Since the GBC standard is 1 bal per second, you combination of gearing, motor and wheel should be capable of revving up after a shot to the required speed within a second. I don't know how high you want to go, but the PF M motor is a weak motor and might not handle higher gearing and recuperation after a shot well. Everything else is a matter of trial and error, took me 3 builds to get a consistent machine.

posts.title: [WIP] Jamestown: A Colonial Redcoat Capital
posts.text: Sharing a few more photos of the display. Here, a sentry guards the entry into town. The campfire behind him was part of the original encampment we build for the Redcoats so I wanted to make sure it made it into this display as well. A JTC Captain inspects the ring he just acquired on his latest voyage. He probably has a special someone in mind. I wonder if she will say yes? I really like the way this side of the display turned out. Working that old Cannon Cove and yellow sand into the newer style bricks was something I wasn't sure would work out aesthetically speaking, but I really think it came together nicely. It looks better in person, of course. I've said it before but taking pictures of Legos is surprisingly difficult. I'll share updates as I make them too. I still have a few roofs and buildings to put the finishing touches on for now, for example. And I need to populate the place a little more. The idea is for this to be a busy city, so I want it to look like one!

posts.title: [WIP] Jamestown: A Colonial Redcoat Capital
posts.text: You sort of read my mind. The initial build was to get it done. From here I'll study building techniques and ways to add the kind of detail you are describing. Chimneys are another detail on my list. I'll also try to add some interior detail, though I'll keep this to a minimum in most cases since you can't see inside most of the buildings. The roof windows was another one I really considered and likely will implement. Lovely thing about Lego. A display like this is never truly done. Another change I may make is replacing the trees with some newer trees to add height. I'm on the fence on this one because I do like the way these old vintage pine trees look.
